pr_snapshot.body:
The four-reference limited-SAD entry point still uses the older dispatcher for each reference. Reuse the fixed-size pointer SIMD kernels for early/partial work. For full scans, share source loads through the existing four-reference SIMD kernel when all limits cover the maximum sum and output is disjoint from inputs/limits. Preserve sequential evaluation whenever stores can affect later reads.

This component currently has no production caller. Retain its verified gains under the project’s explicit kernel-acceptance rule; no whole-codec improvement is claimed.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2 SIMD, PGO off, six fresh permutations:

- Full/wide scans improve **1.634–1.658×** versus current main; all 48 pairs exceed 1.5× (minimum 1.565×).
- Early exits improve **1.908–1.924×**; all 24 pairs exceed 1.5× (minimum 1.854×).
- All 20 cases improve in every pair, with zero allocations. These gains still trail ARM assembly: full scans take 19.7–22.4% more time, early exits about 130% more.

Keep the scalar oracle strict. Legacy ARM NEON returns different threshold witnesses in two patterned mid-exit cases, so preserve the mismatch logs and omit those two ASM timings. The other 18 ASM cases pass the exact oracle. Pinned x64 assembly passes all 20 cases under Rosetta; extend native AMD CI to all 154 kernel cases using identical fixtures. Emulation supplies correctness evidence only.

Validation covers 1,260 four-reference cases, 10 ordered alias arenas, guard adjacency/overlap/nil/stride boundaries, native race/checkptr2, AMD selected/checkptr2 and actual AVX-off, purego/nosimd, and the full native suite. PGO/fingerprint and source/build-selection gates pass. The native PGO-off CLI excludes the limited-x4 entry/guard; its machine text matches the parent after normalizing only the Go build-ID string payload. This is codegen evidence, not a timing claim.

Archive all raw samples, selected/superseded sources, incompatible legacy witnesses and correctness/codegen evidence. Include PR31’s complete native/C audit: EPYC 7763 full-scan slice SAD improves 2.018–2.046×, old early-SAD 1.650×, whole VP8 +0.449% versus main while 13.277% faster than assembly. Separate EPYC 9V74 fixed VP8 takes 2.445× optimized libvpx time at matching measured quality/payload/counts. Preserve the unselected small ARM shift probe separately. README unchanged.

Fresh native x64 CI: EPYC 9V74, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six paired rounds versus main `1a7e69af` and old assembly `691cd051`:
- All 20 new limited-x4 fixtures improve versus main in every pair. Full/wide bounds improve 3.097–3.135x (minimum individual pair 2.768x), early bounds 1.705–1.706x (minimum 1.678x), middle 1.084–1.250x, near 1.068–1.084x. Twelve full/wide/early fixtures exceed 1.5x in every pair.
- Full/wide cases take 34.75–39.22% less time than old assembly. Early still takes 5.53–5.65% more time; middle/near 51.29–91.24% more. All 20 AMD fixtures pass the exact scalar oracle for old assembly, main and current; no AMD cases are excluded. Keep the separate ARM legacy-witness exception limited to the ARM evidence.
- This helper has no production callers. Whole-codec timings are controls: VP8 -0.180% versus main (4/6 faster), but still +11.196% versus assembly in every pair; VP9 320 +0.362% versus main (1/6 faster), VP9 720 -0.473% (3/6 faster), with 41.526%/48.736% less time than assembly respectively. Do not attribute whole-codec differences to this unused helper or claim the 9V74 VP8 gap is closed.
- Unchanged pointer-SAD controls range -0.249% to +0.031% versus main; slice-SAD controls -0.263% to +0.201%. Old early-SAD is +0.012% mixed, still 15.401% slower than assembly. Preserve all 53 median-regressing controls. All-six-slower controls: LoopFilterVerticalEdgesY +0.331%, slice pitch32/patterned/middle +0.201%, Variance16x16 +0.259%.
- All 154 kernel cases have six samples per variant and zero B/op/allocs. Targeted validation passes 78 top-level tests plus six retained panic child probes (84 checks; 106 PASS lines including older subtests), no failures/skips, and main/current SIMD dispatch confirmed. All 22 semantic fields match across three public and two profile datasets; every allocation sample matches, with no outliers.

Separate optimized-C job, also EPYC 9V74: pinned libvpx v1.16.0, runtime dispatch, SSE2/AVX2 and assembly objects enabled. Fixed-speed VP8 takes 2.315x libvpx time at matching measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/encoded and dropped counts; this is not a bitstream-identity assertion. Adaptive VP8 is +81.143% and VP9 +180.597%/+178.641%, with unequal quality/output work. Every quality-pass output statistic matches timed output; reference timing uses vpxenc statistics. These independent job timings do not establish a source effect or support absolute cross-job comparisons.

All three exact-head CI checks pass. Raw artifacts: [native](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39066058781/artifacts/12113184814), [optimized C](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39066058781/artifacts/12113670636).
